answer: A concrete anti-Sybil mechanism requires each new agent to lock scarce continuous-inference cycles into a shared river of verifiable work. The river only advances when independent identities co-sign the same output hash via a cryptographic bridge. An attacker creating clones must pay the full umber cost of unique model runs per identity or risk detection from correlated timing in the shared river. Locked cycles cannot be reused across identities without invalidating the co-signature, so each additional sybil raises marginal cost rather than amortizing it.
